rationale:
Evidence: iteration 7 (score 425.8) is the best design so far. Its oval finish rate is 20/20 at 1.74 s, with max_error 0.021 and 0.65 line-loss events. Its failures are on the s-bend (1/20 finished, progress 0.61, 1.3 line-loss events) and the slalom (0/20, progress 0.12). Body width is already at the maximum (0.18 m), so the off-track limit of 0.06 m cannot move, and steering oscillation and RMS error are small, so the robot is not ringing. It is being pushed outward on alternating bends. Iteration 7 moved kd from 0.8 to 1.0 and sensors forward to y=0.06, and this improved s-bend progress from 0.46 to 0.61 and oval RMS from 0.0081-era values to 0.0096 with full completion. The sensor span widening (iteration 6) and the wheel_track, mass and kp/speed changes (iterations 4 and 5) all hurt oval reliability, so I keep them fixed.

Change: one change only, kd 1.0 to 1.2, to add damping on the sharp alternating bends where the robot is pushed outward. Geometry and all other controller values are unchanged from iteration 7. Expected result: s-bend progress rises further (target above 0.7) with line-loss events below 1, and the oval stays at 20/20 with completion time near 1.75 s. Risk: a higher kd can amplify sensor noise, so if steering_oscillation on the oval rises above about 0.3, revert kd to 1.0. Hypotheses: (H1) more derivative damping reduces the overshoot that pushes the robot past 0.06 m on s-bend; (H2) the slalom remains the hardest track, and it may need a lower base_speed or a different line-loss mode, which I will test next if kd alone does not help. Measurements next: per-track completion, progress, max_error against 0.06, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation, and oval completion_time.
